problems.title: Periodicity and a reciprocal identity
problems.question: Evaluate $(0.99/1.1+0.1)[(1+\cot^2(\pi/10))^{-1}+\cos^2(2011\pi/10)]$.
problems.idea: The decimal factor is 1 and the trig terms are complementary squares.
steps: 2011π/10=201π+π/10, so the cosine square equals cos²(π/10).
The reciprocal term is sin²(π/10), giving total 1.

problems.title: Subtract before reducing a remainder
problems.question: a+2017 leaves remainder 2 on division by 8. Find the remainder of a+2.
problems.idea: The expressions differ by 2015.
steps: Use the remainder between 0 and 7.

problems.title: Count whole discounted books
problems.question: A book costs 19 lari before a 35% reduction. How many can be bought for 100 lari?
problems.idea: Round the quotient down to a whole-book count.
steps: Each costs 12.35 lari.
Eight cost 98.8 lari, while nine cost 111.15.

problems.title: The coordinates give a small parallelogram
problems.question: Parallelogram ABCD has A=(1,2),B=(4,0),D=(2,1). H is the midpoint of AD. Find the area of trapezoid AHCB.
problems.idea: Use the determinant area and the half-side height relation.
steps: B-A=(3,-2),D-A=(1,-1), so the parallelogram area is |-3+2|=1.
AH is half of AD, whereas BC equals AD. The trapezoid shares the parallelogram height between AD and BC.
Its area is (1/2+1)/2=3/4 of the parallelogram area.
problems.answer: 3/4; none of the listed numerical choices.
problems.note: The coordinates yield area 1 for the whole parallelogram, so the listed trapezoid areas above 2 cannot be correct.

problems.title: Possible face angles of a regular nonagonal pyramid
problems.question: Which can be a base angle of a lateral triangular face of a regular nine-sided pyramid: 39°,45°,79°,90°?
problems.idea: A positive height raises the lateral edge above the base-plane circumradius.
formulas: Base side s=2Rsin20°; face base-angle cosine=s/(2L), L>R.
steps: cosβ<sin20°=cos70°, so β>70°.
The face is nondegenerate and isosceles, giving β<90°.
Thus any β in (70°,90°) is possible, and only 79° qualifies.

problems.title: Integer passenger counts expose the wrong choices
problems.question: A bus carries fewer than 100 passengers, with twice as many seated as standing. At a stop 4% leave. How many remain?
problems.idea: Both the seated split and departing count must be integers.
formulas: Passenger count N is divisible by 3; 4%N=N/25 must be an integer.
steps: Thus positive N<100 must be a multiple of lcm(3,25)=75.
So N=75, three leave, and 72 remain.
problems.note: The choices include 3 (the number leaving) and 75 (the initial count), but neither is the number remaining.

problems.title: Use the defining equation inside a logarithm
problems.question: a is the positive root of a¹⁸+a²=1. Find logₐ(a³-a⁵).
problems.idea: Replace 1-a² by a¹⁸.
steps: The equation forces 0<a<1, so the logarithm base is valid.
a³-a⁵=a³a¹⁸=a²¹>0.
The logarithm is therefore 21.

problems.title: The class counts cannot be integers
problems.question: Class I has one more boy and one fewer girl than class II. The girl-sector angle in class II’s pie chart is 30% greater than in class I. Find class I’s size.
problems.idea: The total class sizes are equal, so their sector-angle ratio is the ratio of girl counts.
steps: Let class I have g girls and total N. Class II has g+1 girls and the same total N.
Thus (g+1)/g=1.3, giving g=10/3.
This is impossible for a pupil count. Even without integrality, the equation would not determine N.
problems.answer: No integer class sizes satisfy the stated conditions.
problems.note: The original source says 30%, not 30°. Its data are inconsistent and none of the listed class sizes follows.

problems.title: A periodic equation has no least real root
problems.question: Find the least solution of $(x^2+1)(\cos x+\sin x-6)(1-\sqrt[4]2\sqrt{\sin x})=0$.
problems.idea: The first two factors never vanish over the real domain.
steps: The square root requires sinx≥0. The last factor gives sinx=1/√2.
Hence x=π/4+2πk or 3π/4+2πk, k∈ℤ.
These roots extend indefinitely to negative x, so there is no least real solution. If least nonnegative is intended, it is π/4.
problems.answer: No least real solution; least nonnegative solution π/4.
problems.note: Neither the unrestricted least-root request nor the printed numerical choices supplies the missing nonnegative restriction.

problems.title: Solve a quadratic in cosine
problems.question: Solve 3cosx-cos2x=1.
problems.idea: Use the double-angle formula.
steps: Put c=cosx. Then 3c-2c²+1=1, giving c(3-2c)=0.
c=3/2 is impossible, so cosx=0.
All angles are x=π/2+πk.

problems.title: Two partial sums determine an arithmetic progression
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression S₄=5,S₅=4. Find S₉.
problems.idea: Use the two sum formulas as linear equations.
steps: The equations are 4a+6d=5 and 5a+10d=4.
They give d=-9/10,a=13/5.

problems.title: Smallest positive integer solution sum
problems.question: For positive integer solutions of 9x=4y+1, minimize x+y.
problems.idea: Use the equation modulo 4.
steps: The smallest possible positive x is 1, giving y=2.
Larger solutions have x=1+4k,y=2+9k, k≥0, increasing the sum.

problems.title: Common divisors are divisors of the gcd
problems.question: A is the set of positive divisors of 48 and B those of 64. Find the sum of A∩B.
problems.idea: Find their greatest common divisor.
steps: The positive divisors of 16 are 1,2,4,8,16.
Their sum is 31.
problems.note: This uses the usual school convention of positive divisors. Including negative divisors too would give a sum of zero.

problems.title: Mixture ratio from a weighted percentage
problems.question: Alloys contain p% and q% copper. In what mass ratio should they be mixed to make z%?
problems.idea: Equate the copper masses.
steps: Rearrange to (p-z)m₁=(z-q)m₂.
Thus m₁/m₂=(z-q)/(p-z), assuming p≠z and positive masses.
For both masses positive, z must lie strictly between distinct p,q. Endpoint percentages require one mass to vanish; if p=q=z, every ratio works.
problems.answer: First:second mass ratio = (z-q):(p-z), with the stated feasibility conditions.

problems.title: Absolute-value inputs double positive roots
problems.question: f(x)=0 has exactly five roots, three positive and two negative. How many roots has f(|x|)=0?
problems.idea: An absolute value cannot reach a negative root.
steps: The two negative original roots give no solutions.
Each of the three positive roots gives two distinct opposite x-values.
There is no zero root among the stated five.

problems.title: A function and its inverse meet only at zero
problems.question: Which listed point lies on both y=3x and its inverse?
problems.idea: The inverse is y=x/3.
steps: The equality gives 8x=0, hence x=0,y=0.
The only intersection is (0,0), absent from the choices.

problems.title: Equal edges do not force a right prism
problems.question: All edges of a triangular prism are equal. Find the acute angle between skew diagonals of two lateral faces.
problems.idea: Separate a right regular prism from an oblique prism.
steps: If the prism is right, take unit base-edge vectors u,v with u·v=-1/2 and vertical unit vector w perpendicular to both.
Directions of suitable skew face diagonals are u+w and v+w, with dot product 1/2 and both lengths √2. Their acute angle has cosine 1/4.
But equal edge lengths also allow an oblique unit vector w. Then u·w and v·w can vary, changing the diagonal lengths and their angle.
problems.answer: For a right regular prism: $\arccos(1/4)$. With only equal edges: the angle is not uniquely determined.
problems.note: The question does not explicitly state that the prism is right. None of the listed angles equals arccos(1/4); arctan(1/4) is a different value.

problems.title: A whole half-line solves the parameter equation
problems.question: Solve $(2|a|^3+a^3)/(|a|^3-a^3)=1/2$.
problems.idea: Check the denominator in each sign case.
steps: If a≥0 the denominator is zero, so the expression is undefined.
If a<0, the numerator is -a³ and denominator -2a³, giving exactly 1/2.
Thus every negative a works.
problems.note: The numerical choice -5 is one solution, but it is not the complete solution set requested.

problems.title: Equal areas of a cube and sphere
problems.question: A cube and sphere have equal surface areas. Find cube volume divided by sphere volume.
problems.idea: Eliminate the radius using the area equation.
steps: The area equality gives a/R=√(2π/3).
Simplification gives √(π/6).

problems.title: No listed construction is always odd
problems.question: For every real-domain function f, which listed construction is odd: f(x⁵), f(x)+f(-x), f(-x), or the repeated f(x)+f(-x)?
problems.idea: A single counterexample can reject a universal claim.
steps: Choose f(x)=1 for every x. The constructions become the nonzero constant functions 1,2,1,2, none odd.
The sum f(x)+f(-x) is always even; its repeated appearance does not make it odd.
A generally odd construction would be f(x)-f(-x), but that is absent.
problems.answer: None of the listed constructions is always odd.
problems.note: Two choices are identical sums. The likely intended difference is not what the source actually prints.

problems.title: Midpoint cuts halve two triangle areas
problems.question: K,L are the midpoints of CD,AB in convex quadrilateral ABCD. Find area AKCL in terms of total area S.
problems.idea: Split both quadrilaterals along diagonal AC.
formulas: A triangle with half a base and the same altitude has half the area.
steps: Triangle AKC is half of triangle ADC because CK=CD/2.
Triangle ALC is half of triangle ABC because AL=AB/2.
Their union is AKCL, so its area is half the original total.

problems.title: A logarithmic inequality needs a positive argument
problems.question: Solve log₂(x²-6x)≤4.
problems.idea: Impose both lower and upper bounds on the argument.
steps: The positive-argument condition gives x<0 or x>6.
The upper bound x²-6x-16≤0 gives -2≤x≤8.
Their intersection is [-2,0)∪(6,8].
problems.note: None of the printed numerical intervals matches this set.

problems.title: Recover the original side ratio
problems.question: A rectangle’s length rises 20%, width 60%, and perimeter 28%. Find original length/width.
problems.idea: Perimeter depends on a sum, not the area product.
steps: Rearrange to 0.08L=0.32W.
Thus L/W=4.

problems.title: A trapezoid section through its diagonal crossing
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 8 m and 12 m. Find the segment parallel to them through the diagonal intersection, between the legs.
problems.idea: Its length is the harmonic mean of the bases.
steps: The diagonal intersection is fraction b/(a+b) of the height from the b-base toward the a-base. Linear interpolation gives b+(a-b)b/(a+b)=2ab/(a+b).
For a=8,b=12, the length is 192/20=9.6.

problems.title: Cosine of 45 plus 30 degrees
problems.question: Find cos75°.
problems.idea: Use the cosine addition formula.

problems.title: Changing both a base and its exponent
problems.question: For $f(x)=((500+4x)/(500-4x))^{7/x}$, find f(57)/f(-57).
problems.idea: Negating x reciprocates the base and negates the exponent.
steps: Both bases at ±57 are positive because 500-228>0.
Their ratio is 1.

problems.title: Area of a region defined by three inequalities
problems.question: Find the area satisfying x≤y+3, y+2x≥0, y≤0.
problems.idea: Intersect the three boundary lines.
formulas: The bounds are y≥x-3,y≥-2x,y≤0; triangle area=base·height/2.
steps: The boundary vertices are (0,0),(3,0),(1,-2).
The horizontal base has length 3 and the height is 2.
The area is 3·2/2=3.

problems.title: Overlap of squares rotated about a vertex
problems.question: A square of side a rotates 45° around a vertex. Find the common area with the original square.
problems.idea: Use coordinates and integrate the overlap width.
formulas: Original 0≤x,y≤a; rotated constraints include y≥x and x+y≤√2a.
steps: For 0≤y≤a, the overlap has 0≤x≤min(y,√2a-y). The bounds switch at y=a/√2.
The first integral is a²/4 and the second is a²(√2-5/4), giving total a²(√2-1).

problems.title: A divisibility condition with negative integers
problems.question: Find the sum of all integers n for which (n²+6n-8)/(n+3) is integral.
problems.idea: Divide the polynomial first.
steps: The denominator n+3 must be a divisor of 17: ±1,±17.
Their sum is -12.

problems.title: Choose the positive radical sign
problems.question: If $\sqrt{21-12\sqrt3}=x+y\sqrt3$ with integers x,y, find x+y.
problems.idea: Recognize a perfect square, then enforce the nonnegative square root.
steps: Since 2√3>3, the square root is 2√3-3.
Thus x=-3,y=2 and x+y=-1.
The opposite signs x=3,y=-2 give the negative root and are invalid.

problems.title: A train passes a point and a platform
problems.question: A train passes a stationary observer in 7 seconds and a 306 m platform in 25 seconds. Find its speed and length.
problems.idea: Passing a platform adds its full length to the distance.
steps: Subtract to get 306=18v, so v=17 m/s.
Then L=119 m. Multiply the speed by 3.6 to get 61.2 km/h.

problems.title: An exponential substitution after matching logarithms
problems.question: Solve $\log_{1/3}(6^{-x})=\log_3(4^x-12\cdot9^x)$.
problems.idea: The left side equals log₃(6ˣ).
formulas: log_(1/3)u=-log₃u; equal valid logarithms have equal arguments.
steps: The equation becomes 6ˣ=4ˣ-12·9ˣ. Divide by 9ˣ>0.
Set t=(2/3)ˣ>0. Then t=t²-12, giving (t-4)(t+3)=0.
Only t=4 is positive, so x=log_(2/3)4. At this x the original right argument equals 6ˣ>0.

problems.title: Factor using the Pythagorean identity
problems.question: Solve 3cos²x+4sin2x-sin²x=3.
problems.idea: Replace sin2x and also write the constant 3 as 3(sin²x+cos²x).
steps: After moving 3 across, the equation is 8sinxcosx-4sin²x=0.
Factor 4sinx(2cosx-sinx)=0.
The first branch gives x=πk. The second gives tanx=2; cosx cannot vanish on that branch.

problems.title: Keep the root before cancelling a common factor
problems.question: Solve 2-3x+x²=2(x-1)√x.
problems.idea: Factor first; dividing by x-1 would lose a solution.
steps: The domain is x≥0. Rewrite as (x-1)(x-2-2√x)=0.
One solution is x=1. For the second factor put t=√x≥0: t²-2t-2=0.
Only t=1+√3 is nonnegative, giving x=(1+√3)²=4+2√3.

problems.title: Internal division of a vector segment
problems.question: In pyramid DABC, M∈AB and AM:MB=2:5. With DA=a, DB=b, DC=c, express vector MC.
problems.idea: Use D as the position-vector origin.
steps: Since M is 2/7 of the way from A to B, DM=a+(2/7)(b-a)=(5a+2b)/7.
Subtract DM from DC.

problems.title: A horizontal chord inside a cone
problems.question: A cone has slant 13 cm and height 12 cm. A line parallel to its base is 6 cm above the base and 2 cm from its axis. Find the chord inside the cone.
problems.idea: Similarity gives the circular section radius at that height.
formulas: Base r=√(L²-h²); section radius scales with remaining height; chord=2√(ρ²-d²).
steps: The base radius is √(169-144)=5.
At height 6 of 12, the section radius is 5/2.
The chord length is 2√[(5/2)²-2²]=2·3/2=3.
problems.note: The printed final phrase is malformed. This interprets its “2 cm” as the line’s distance from the cone height/axis; reading it as a second cone height would contradict the stated 12 cm.

problems.title: An arithmetic progression from quotient conditions
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression, a₉/a₂=5 and dividing a₁₃ by a₆ gives quotient 2, remainder 5. Find the first term and difference.
problems.idea: Translate the quotient statements into equations.
steps: The first gives a+8d=5(a+d), so 3d=4a.
The second gives a+12d=2(a+5d)+5, so 2d-a=5.
Substitute a=3d/4 to get 5d/4=5, hence d=4,a=3. The divisor a₆=23 exceeds remainder 5 as required.

problems.title: Four tangent spheres resting on a plane
problems.question: Three unit spheres rest on a plane and touch pairwise. A fourth sphere rests on the same plane and touches all three. Find a large sphere’s volume divided by the small sphere’s surface area.
problems.idea: The fourth centre lies above the circumcentre of the three unit-sphere centres.
formulas: Equilateral side 2 has circumradius 2/√3; external tangency gives centre distance R+1.
steps: If the fourth radius is R, its vertical separation from the unit-sphere centres is R-1.
Pythagoras gives (R+1)²=(R-1)²+4/3, so 4R=4/3 and R=1/3.
A unit sphere volume is 4π/3; the small sphere surface area is 4π/9. Their ratio is 3.

problems.title: Count integers in an exponential-logarithmic range
problems.question: How many integers are in the range of $16\log_{1/16}[(\sin x+\cos x+3\sqrt2)/\sqrt2]$?
problems.idea: Bound the argument before applying the decreasing logarithm.
steps: The argument ranges over [2,4].
The logarithm ranges over [-1/2,-1/4], and multiplication by 16 gives [-8,-4].
The integers are -8,-7,-6,-5,-4.

problems.title: An integer parameter keeps the discriminant away from zero
problems.question: For integer k making x²+(k-10)x+9=0 have two distinct real roots, minimize x₁²+x₂².
problems.idea: Express the target and distinct-root condition using k.
steps: Distinct real roots require |k-10|>6. Since k is an integer, the smallest possible magnitude is 7.
The least squared sum is 7²-18=31.
It is attained at k=3 or 17, both having positive discriminant 13.
